about.title: About BIZSIM
about.lead: An open-source platform for learning strategy by making real decisions, with evidence, sources and honest uncertainty.
about.how1: All 200 catalogue seasons are built in and play offline. Every season follows six steps: Situation, Concept, Evidence, Episodes, Outcome and Insight. Each episode holds two to four linked decisions and ends with its own outcome and insight; later episodes build on earlier ones. Pre-decision material is written so it does not reveal the answer. Historical outcomes cite their sources. Alternatives you did not see play out are clearly marked as counterfactual assessments.
about.how2: Decisions are judged on process quality, how sound they were given what was known, not on hindsight. Matching history is reported separately, because history was sometimes wrong.
about.kindsAi: Seasons written by an AI model (live research and the chat builder) carry an AI-written label and name the model.
about.evidenceMethod: Each historical outcome and evidence figure in the built-in seasons was compared automatically with the text of the source it cites: its years, figures and proper names were searched for in that source. This shows whether the source states the same details. It does not prove the history is true, and sources can be wrong or disputed.
about.provVerified: Structured data or official filings, as published, with a link
about.provSource: Source reference, encyclopedias, publishers, the company’s own site
about.provAi: AI-generated analysis, interpretation by a language model, grounded in cited sources
about.provHypo: Hypothetical scenario, possible futures, not facts
data: Wikidata (CC0) and Wikipedia (CC BY-SA) for company profiles
U.S. SEC EDGAR for audited financials and filings
Google News, Bing News or GDELT for recent headlines (links only)
Wikipedia and Wikimedia Commons for each season's own lead image, free licenses only (credited on use)
Piper open-source voice engine with public-domain / CC0 male voices
Optional: Gemini or OpenAI image generation, always labeled as AI
about.languages: The interface is available in {{count}} languages. English is the source language. All other languages, including British English spellings, were machine-assisted and have not been reviewed by native speakers yet; the status of each is shown in Settings. Built-in seasons are written in English; a small sample has a machine-assisted translation.
about.install: On iPhone or iPad: open BIZSIM in Safari, tap Share, then “Add to Home Screen”. On Android: open it in Chrome and choose “Install app”. On Windows, macOS and Linux: use the browser’s install button, or the desktop app built from the source. See README.md for desktop and native mobile builds.
about.license: BIZSIM is released under the MIT license. Book principles are short paraphrases for educational commentary; the books remain the property of their authors and publishers.
about.privacy: No accounts, no tracking, no subscriptions. Your progress stays on your device.

transfer.damaged: The transfer code is incomplete or damaged.
transfer.empty: The transfer code holds no BIZSIM data.

send.title: Send progress to another device
send.intro: On the other device open BIZSIM, Settings, Receive progress, and point the camera at this screen. Turn the brightness up and keep both devices steady until every code is captured.
send.includeCases: Include generated and built cases (more codes)
send.copied: Transfer code copied. Paste it on the other device.
send.copyBlocked: Copy is blocked here. Use the QR codes instead.
send.privacy: Nothing is uploaded. Codes contain only your BIZSIM progress and library, compressed.

receive.title: Receive progress
receive.isPairing: That is a pairing code. Use Connect to a computer for it.
receive.isSeason: That is a shared season. Use Import a season (in My cases or Settings) for it.
receive.partial: {{got}} of {{n}} codes captured. Add the rest.
receive.done: Merged into this device: {{summary}}. Nothing on this device was deleted.
receive.intro: On the other device open Settings → Send progress, then scan the moving QR codes here.

panel.title: Move to another device
panel.intro: Switching between phone, tablet and computer? Transfer your decisions, profile, saved companies and cases with QR codes, offline, no account. Progress is merged, never overwritten.
panel.single: To share a single season or episode, open it and choose Share.

pair.isTransfer: That is a transfer code, not a pairing code. Use Receive for it.
pair.title: Connect to a computer
pair.done: Connected to BIZSIM at {{origin}}. Live research and case building now run on your computer while both devices are on the same Wi‑Fi. You can remove this device on the computer at any time.
pair.intro: On your computer open BIZSIM → Settings → Use on your phone, turn it on, and scan the code it shows. Each code works once and expires after five minutes.
pair.pasteInstead: {{problem}} Paste the pairing link shown on the computer instead.

phone.title: Use on your phone
phone.intro: Let your phone or tablet use this computer’s BIZSIM (live research, case building and your API keys) over the same Wi‑Fi. Each pairing code works once and expires after five minutes. Paired devices sign every request; you can remove them here at any time.
phone.qrAlt: Pairing QR code for your phone
phone.expires: Code expires in {{time}}. A new one appears automatically.
phone.scanWith: Scan with the BIZSIM phone app (Settings → Connect to a computer), or with the phone’s camera to open BIZSIM in its browser.
phone.firewall: If the phone cannot connect, allow BIZSIM through your computer’s firewall when asked. Traffic on your Wi‑Fi is signed but not encrypted, so use phone access on networks you trust.
phone.noNetwork: This computer is not connected to a private network (home or office Wi‑Fi).

computer.title: Connect to a computer
computer.intro: Running BIZSIM on a computer too? Pair with it to use its live research and case building from this device over Wi‑Fi.

share.title: Share this season
share.intro: On the other device open My cases → Import a season and scan these codes, or send the .bizsim file. Only the season content is shared: never your progress, keys or settings.
share.integrityNote: . The integrity check detects damaged transfers; it does not prove who made a file or that its content is accurate.

import.title: Import a season
import.otherPackage: These codes belong to a different season than the ones already scanned. Finish the first one, or cancel to start again.
import.isProgress: That is a progress transfer, not a season. Use Settings → Receive progress.
import.isPairing: That is a pairing code. Use Settings → Connect to a computer.
import.confirmReplace: Replace your copy of “{{title}}” with the imported version? Your earlier runs stay in your history.
import.intactHint: The package structure and integrity check passed. This does not prove who made it or that it is accurate.
import.trust: . Imported seasons come from whoever shared them: check the sources before relying on them.
import.cleaned_one: {{count}} item was cleaned during the check
import.cleaned_other: {{count}} items were cleaned during the check
import.builtin: This season is already built into BIZSIM. Nothing needs importing.
import.identical: You already have this exact season.
import.conflict: You have a different version of this season (“{{title}}”). Keep both, or replace yours. Nothing changes until you choose.
import.intro: Scan the codes shown on the other device (Share this season), or open a .bizsim file. Imported files are checked before anything is saved.
import.capturedSaved: Codes captured (saved, you can continue later)

report.ai: AI disclosure: this season was written by an AI model from the cited sources. Check important facts in the sources.
report.aiModel: AI disclosure: this season was written by an AI model ({{model}}) from the cited sources. Check important facts in the sources.
report.open: Outcome: none recorded. This decision is still open, so there is no documented result.
report.matched: Matched history: {{matched}} of {{total}} documented decisions. Matching history is not a grade: history was sometimes wrong.
report.matchedNone: Matched history: not applicable (no documented outcomes in this attempt).
report.avg: Average process quality: {{avg}} of 3, judged on what was known at the time, not on how things turned out.
report.avgNone: Average process quality: no decisions yet.
report.noReflection: No reflection written for this attempt.
report.evidenceNote: Evidence statuses come from an automated check that looks for each claim’s dates, figures and names in the cited source text. A match shows the source states the same details; it does not prove the history.
